newsitem.title: UK: U.S. grain prices up on crop data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grain prices up on crop data.

text.p: Bellwether U.S. wheat futures advanced almost to the $4 per bushel barrier on Friday on government data that reported the lowest American winter wheat plantings since 1978. The U.S. Department of Agriculture said 48.2 million acres were seeded with winter wheat, compared with trade expectations of 50 to 53 million.
Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) March wheat futures traded as high as 399-3/4 cents per bushel, up almost 10 cents, before profit taking.

The nearby contract was last at $4 on December 20. Current values compare with a record $7.50 last March at a time when drought in several nations depressed world grain stocks to their lowest for 20 years. Bumper 1996 harvests later sent wheat prices sliding but they have steadied in recent days.
The U.S. farm data on Friday also showed December 1 U.S. wheat stocks still at their lowest in a decade and down by 9 percent from a year ago.

Soybean production for 1996 was also seen below expectations at 2.38 billion bushels and soybean futures jumped almost 30 cents at one point to $7.25 per bushel. Gold prices steadied on Friday from a dramatic New Year slide that had taken them down by 3-1/2 percent since the end of 1996.

Dealers said Japanese buying kicked in early, and that bullion was later supported by U.S. jobs data that pointed to a robust economy and triggered speculation of a rise in U.S. interest rates. Gold was fixed in London's afternoon at $358.25 per ounce, up from traded 3-1/4 year lows below $354 on Thursday.
Oil prices paused in their cold weather rally and profit taking also took copper and aluminium down slightly from values seen in rallies, based on tight stocks, during the week.
But coffee prices continued to be buoyed by supply concerns. Some leading commodity prices at 1700 GMT Friday -
